dialogue.title: Getting an Oregon Driver's License
dialogue.context: Ahmed goes to the DMV to get his Oregon driver's license. He talks to a DMV clerk.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Next! How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Hi, I need to get an Oregon driver's license. I have a license from Somalia but not a U.S. one.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Okay, you'll need to take both the written test and the driving test. First, what documents do you have?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I have my passport, my work permit, and two bills showing my Oregon address.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Perfect. That's everything we need. The written test costs $90. If you pass, you can schedule your driving test.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Can I take the written test today?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Yes, you can take it right now on the computer. It's 35 questions and you need to get 28 correct to pass.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Is it in English? My English is okay but not perfect.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: We have the test in many languages including Arabic and Somali. Which would you prefer?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I'll try it in English first. If I fail, can I retake it?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Yes, you can retake it after 24 hours. You get three attempts included in the $90 fee. Let me get you set up.

listening_exercises.transcript: To get an Oregon driver's license, you need: proof of identity like a passport, proof of Social Security number, and two documents showing your Oregon address. You must pass a vision test, a written knowledge test with 35 questions, and a driving skills test. The license costs $90 and is valid for 8 years.
listening_exercises.question: How many years is an Oregon driver's license valid?

listening_exercises.transcript: The DMV written test covers traffic laws, road signs, and safe driving practices. You can take a practice test online at oregon.gov/odot. Study the Oregon Driver Manual before taking the test. The test is available in English, Spanish, Russian, Chinese, Vietnamese, and other languages.
listening_exercises.question: Where can you take a practice test?

listening_exercises.transcript: For the driving test, bring a properly insured and registered vehicle. The examiner will check your lights, signals, brakes, and horn. The test takes about 20 minutes and includes parking, turning, and highway driving. If you fail, you must wait at least one week before retesting.
listening_exercises.question: How long must you wait to retake the driving test if you fail?

speaking_tasks.prompt: You're at the DMV. Ask: 'I need to get a driver's license. What documents do I need? How much does it cost? Can I take the test today?' Record yourself.
speaking_tasks.example: Hello, I need to get an Oregon driver's license. I'm new to Oregon. What documents do I need to bring? Also, how much does the license cost? And can I take the written test today, or do I need an appointment? Thank you.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Explain the steps to get a driver's license in the U.S. Give at least 4 steps. Talk for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: To get a driver's license, you need to follow several steps. First, gather your documents - passport, social security card, and proof of address. Second, study the driver's manual and take practice tests online. Third, go to the DMV and take the written test. If you pass, fourth, schedule and take the driving test. Finally, if you pass the driving test, you'll get your license. The whole process can take a few weeks.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write a list of 5 documents you might need to bring to the DMV. Then write 2 sentences explaining why these documents are important.
writing_tasks.example: Documents needed for the DMV: 1) Passport or birth certificate, 2) Social Security card, 3) Utility bill with your address, 4) Bank statement with your address, 5) Work permit or visa if not a U.S. citizen. These documents are important because the DMV needs to verify your identity and confirm that you live in Oregon. Without the correct documents, you cannot get a license.

writing_tasks.prompt: Imagine you failed your driving test. Write an email to your friend explaining what happened and what you'll do next. (4-5 sentences)
writing_tasks.example: Hi Maria, I took my driving test today but I didn't pass. I was too nervous and made some mistakes with parallel parking. The examiner was nice and told me what I need to practice. I have to wait one week before I can try again. I'm going to practice parking every day this week. Wish me luck! Ahmed

grammar_focus.title: 'Need to' for Requirements
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'need to' to talk about things that are required or necessary.
examples: I need to get a driver's license. (requirement)
You need to bring two forms of ID. (necessary)
He needs to pass the written test first. (requirement)
Do I need to make an appointment? (asking about requirement)

practice.sentence: You ___ to take the vision test.

grammar_focus.title: Conditional Questions with 'If'
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'if' to ask about conditions or possibilities. 'If + present, can/will + base verb'
examples: If I pass, can I drive today? (condition + question)
If I fail, will I get a refund? (condition + question)
If I move, do I need a new license? (condition + question)
What happens if I don't pass? (asking about consequence)

practice.sentence: If I ___ the test, can I retake it?
If you pass, you ___ get your license.
___ I lose my license, what do I do?

grammar_focus.title: Future Arrangements with 'When can I...?'
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'When can I...?' to ask about scheduling or arranging things in the future.
examples: When can I schedule my test? (arranging future appointment)
When can I pick up my license? (future action)
When can I retake the exam? (future possibility)
When can I drive with my permit? (asking about timing)

cultural_notes: In the U.S., each state issues its own driver's licenses. If you move states, you usually need to get a new license within 30-90 days.
DMV wait times can be very long (2-4 hours). Making an appointment online saves time.
Most states accept foreign driver's licenses for a short time (30-90 days), but then you need a U.S. license.
The written test is available in many languages, so you don't have to take it in English.
If you're under 18, you need a learner's permit first and must have supervised driving hours.
Car insurance is REQUIRED in all states. Driving without insurance can result in fines and license suspension.
